reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape: nothing is proposed to the counterparty, so there is no risk of a directionally wrong or over-reaching edit.

The cited text supports the classification: Section 6.3(a)(i)-(ii) is a counterparty-side (Servicer/Marketing Agent) indemnity running in favour of the Issuer and trustees for willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, including enforcement costs; 6.3(b) supplies standard notice/defence/separate-counsel procedure and 6.3(c) survival. The indemnity is uncapped and no reciprocal indemnity of the Servicer is cited, so our side is not exposed — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap.

The failed deterministic check (no IP-infringement indemnity) is correctly treated as a noted sub-element rather than a deviation: this is a receivables securitisation transfer and servicing agreement with no licensed services or deliverables, so an IP indemnity is commercially inapposite and its absence is not a material failure of the fallback on the terms that actually operate here.

Rationale is accurate to the quoted paragraphs and transparently flags the residual gaps (no standalone breach-of-law or data-disclosure trigger, Depositor not named as an Indemnified Person) as informational, which is the correct handling for a retained compliance record.
